battlecards.why_selected: Quoted a 2.56% net effective rate vs. incumbent 2.86%; projected >$550K annual savings; offered agnostic technology stack, strong customer service and interchange optimization support.
battlecards.contract_terms: Pricing to be memorialized post-award; month-to-month with option to exit incumbent Chase once Calibr live; 3-5 year enterprise value modeled on savings.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Provided Chase’s detailed 12-month statement to all bidders; credible switching intent and PE-backed mandate for 10%+ savings.
supplier_strengths: Ability to further optimize interchange after go-live
supplier_weaknesses: Limited track record with Christian-focused retailers
battlecards.switching_costs: Re-tokenizing stored cards, migrating subscription/MIT framework, re-certifying payment pages; estimated 4–6 week IT effort.
battlecards.notes: Treya to schedule implementation kickoff; Calibr believes additional savings possible after first quarter review.

battlecards.why_not_selected: Refused to improve 2.86% net effective rate; potential future increases; lost on price and service flexibility.
battlecards.contract_terms: Monthly evergreen agreement; no minimum volume commitments.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: 30-year tenure created complacency; competitive bids exposed 30 bps over-market pricing.
supplier_weaknesses: Slow to innovate per client feedback
battlecards.switching_costs: Minimal due to month-to-month terms, but card token migration required.
battlecards.notes: Treya will notify Chase of non-renewal once Calibr contract executed.

battlecards.why_selected: Lowest all-in bid (25-31% below incumbent); flexible 3-month trial, technology portal for real-time quoting, favorable fuel inclusive rates.
battlecards.contract_terms: 3-month pilot beginning mid-Jan 2025; no volume commitments; contract to be finalized post-pilot with option for 12-month fixed linehaul matrix.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Incumbent contract expiring 2/28/25 with no penalties; market rates down >20%; competitive RFP data.
supplier_weaknesses: Requires process change for load tendering
battlecards.switching_costs: Carrier onboarding, updating routing guide in WMS, staff training on Echo portal.
battlecards.notes: Performance to be reviewed after February to confirm long-term award.

battlecards.why_not_selected: Pricing 15-25% above market benchmarks; would not meet target reductions during renewal discussions.
battlecards.contract_terms: Rates effective until 2/28/2025; no minimum volume clause allowed easy exit.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Threat of full shift to Echo, RFP results shared.
battlecards.switching_costs: Minimal due to no volume commitments; internal comfort level with OD operations lost.
battlecards.notes: Christianbook may retain OD as secondary backup carrier for peak periods.

battlecards.why_selected: Provided lowest cost on majority of lanes; enabled consolidation of fragmented carrier base; aligns with parallel LTL award for administrative simplicity.
battlecards.contract_terms: Spot-quote model with quarterly rate reviews; no fuel schedule deviations allowed; performance KPIs tracked during Q1 trial.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Bundling FTL and LTL volume; ability to shift lanes immediately post-peak season.
supplier_weaknesses: Service performance yet to be proven
battlecards.switching_costs: Lane set-up in TMS, updating carrier master list, credit app processing.
battlecards.notes: Echo to start quoting FTL lanes in parallel with LTL pilot beginning January.

battlecards.why_selected: Met target pricing while retaining >50% of business to honor prior contractual commitments; offered quickest implementation (1/1/2025).
battlecards.contract_terms: Pricing effective 1/1/2025 with quarterly OCC index review; volume share >50% for duration of 12-month agreement.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Threat of shifting volume to new entrant Key Container; full usage data shared across bidders.
supplier_weaknesses: Initial quote above market, required multiple rounds to meet targets
battlecards.switching_costs: New die-cuts and pallet patterns if moved; potential line downtime.
battlecards.notes: Savings represents combined reductions on CB#1 and CB#3 cartons.

battlecards.why_selected: Most competitive pricing on high-volume CB #5A carton; diversified supply base and added leverage over incumbents.
battlecards.contract_terms: Pricing live 12/13/2024; no minimum volume but expected share ~26% of category spend.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Willingness to pilot new supplier for price relief; incumbents aware of potential shift.
supplier_weaknesses: New relationship – quality and lead-time performance untested
battlecards.switching_costs: Tooling for new SKU already produced; limited additional costs.
battlecards.notes: Continued qualification during Q1 to monitor quality metrics before long-term commitment.
